question:
A 64-year-old woman visits her primary care physician due to a progressively worsening cough. She
reports having had the cough for 5 months, with increased frequency and production of yellow sputum
over the past 2 weeks. She also notes worsening baseline dyspnea on exertion but denies fever,
hemoptysis, or chest pain. Her medical history includes chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
and mild osteoarthritis. She uses inhaled ipratropium and takes ibuprofen as needed. She received the
influenza vaccine 2 months ago. She smokes half a pack of cigarettes daily and denies alcohol or
recreational drug use. Along with broad-spectrum antibiotics, which of the following vaccinations is
recommended for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Vaccination to promote cytokine-mediated
macrophage activation (B) Vaccination to target intracellular pathogens through CD8+ T-cell activation

(C) Vaccination to enhance memory B-cell activation against encapsulated bacteria (D) Vaccination to
stimulate long-term immunity via dendritic cell priming (E) Vaccination to induce a B-cell response with
moderate level affinity antibodies (F) Vaccination with a live attenuated virus to stimulate cellular
immunity (G) Vaccination with a polysaccharide antigen to stimulate T-cell independent immunity (H)
Vaccination to induce a T-cell dependent B-cell response with high affinity antibodies (I) Vaccination
composed of a protein-based surface antigen (J) Vaccination to induce mucosal immunity via IgA
production
 A. Vaccination to induce a T-cell dependent B-cell response with high affinity antibodies
B. Vaccination to stimulate long-term immunity via dendritic cell priming
C. Vaccination to target intracellular pathogens through CD8+ T-cell activation
D. Vaccination with a live attenuated virus to stimulate cellular immunity
E. Vaccination with a polysaccharide antigen to stimulate T-cell independent immunity
F. Vaccination to induce a B-cell response with moderate level affinity antibodies
G. Vaccination composed of a protein-based surface antigen
H. Vaccination to enhance memory B-cell activation against encapsulated bacteria
I. Vaccination to induce mucosal immunity via IgA production
J. Vaccination to promote cytokine-mediated macrophage activation
